issues.title: Track accepted HydrAMP resource: scientific comparison, standalone review and future directions
issues.body:
## Purpose and investigator direction

The investigators accept the exact modern HydrAMP dev3 resource for **experimental AMP generation** following the bounded review in https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/8#issuecomment-6618984173. Record the disposition under D41; this is acceptance of the reviewed resource and route, not general scientific equivalence, biological effectiveness or release readiness.

This new issue owns **future consumer follow-up** after #8's qualification/disposition. It does not reopen #8's completed tests or duplicate the fork's [numerical investigation](https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/1) or [descriptive-profile proposal](https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/2).

## Work to retain

1. Review whether modern and original HydrAMP are comparable in scientific outputs: define operational and biological endpoints separately, reuse retained paired evidence, and design prospective criteria before any new benchmark.
2. Review the modern fork as an independent scientific product: standalone usability, documented definitions and limits, reproducibility, tests, provenance, installation and release prerequisites.
3. Assess whether the approach can support other peptide families or seed a distinct family-extensible method. Existing AMP weights are not qualified for CPP or any new function merely because inference was modernized.
4. Consider a factual handoff to the original authors and assess their interest. Modernization may be useful independently of whether a new algorithm is justified. **No external contact, issue, comment or PR is authorized by recording this item.**

The independently closable provider work belongs in uibcdf/hydramp:

- [Design a prospective scientific-output comparison of modern and original HydrAMP](https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/3).
- [Review modern HydrAMP as an independent scientific software product](https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4).
- [Assess whether HydrAMP can seed a family-extensible peptide-generation method](https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/5).
- [Prepare a possible handoff to original HydrAMP authors and assess collaboration interest](https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/6).

PeptideMT owns consumption, design questions, orchestration and interpretation; molecular operations remain MolSysMT-owned.

## Current evidence and boundaries

Provider wheel SHA-256: `81761e0d48d92f0956e0afc28b3b4154f16032de53c666fd2cfbb53606102ed7`.
Consumer wheel SHA-256: `18b1cb18b9662092203aad9c64d45bc0d61a862577297c13a664572dbdbc3e83`.
Local report: `devguide/hydramp_dev3_acceptance_review.md`.

Preserve the 256-input sequence/batch fidelity, retained probability/global-rank FAILs, selected FP64 evidence (91 modern /58 original /43 equal), private H4 composition and separate real installed public generation case. Zero of 30 compatible H4 proposals has joint Macrel AMP-positive/NonHemo labels. No general efficacy, superiority or all-public live workflow proof follows. Starter-versus-Drive asset byte identity remains unverified.

## Completion and execution authority

- Link the provider-owned issues and record each accept/defer/decline outcome and its evidence.
- After acceptance recording, maintain an honest generation→assessment→selection tutorial using retained receipts first; cached replay must not be labelled new model execution.
- A consumer benchmark or new provider adoption gets a concrete scientific design and exact resource/call review before execution.
- Preserve existing D35/M1–M8 and the Macrel-based selectors; no new HydrAMP-score prefilter or silent score/chemistry change.
- This issue commissions tracking and review proposals, **not** training, new models/families, another inference campaign, GPU, package/model publication or outreach. Existing scientific allowances are exhausted.

issues.title: Design a prospective scientific-output comparison of modern and original HydrAMP
issues.body:
## Question

Can modern HydrAMP be shown comparable to the original in scientifically meaningful results, beyond finite software/sequence fidelity? Define what “comparable” means before collecting new outcomes; do not use an unchanged sequence pool, high native AMP scores or agreement with Macrel as independent biological proof.

## Existing evidence to reuse

The 256-input campaign preserves all observed generated token/sequence/batch return views, with retained probability and global near-tie ranking FAILs. The selected 192-row FP64 investigation favors modern aggregate numerical error, while original is closer for 58 rows. The two H4 seed pools match retained original sequences but yield zero joint Macrel AMP-positive/NonHemo hits among 30 compatible strings. These are finite and partly selected fixtures, not a representative efficacy benchmark. Numerical causality/precision remains independently tracked in #1.

## Proposed review and completion criteria

- Separate fixed-input implementation fidelity, prediction performance, generation utility/diversity/novelty and reproducibility/resource observations.
- Inventory appropriate published evaluation material and permitted use; inspect assay endpoints/units, chemistry, duplicate handling and training overlap before choosing a held-out benchmark. Reuse training examples only for regression claims.
- Predeclare comparators, matched assets/inputs, sample sizes, occurrence/tie handling, metrics, practical equivalence margins where defensible, uncertainty and stopping rules. A failure to detect a difference is not proof of equivalence.
- Preserve unfavorable outcomes and distinguish computational predictions from experimental activity/safety. Keep deployment speed observations separate from scientific quality.
- Deliver a reviewable prospective protocol and a justified accept/narrow/defer decision; any later execution gets its own exact finite host/call authorization.

issues.title: Review modern HydrAMP as an independent scientific software product
issues.body:
## Purpose

Give the modern fork a systematic review as an independently usable scientific tool, rather than relying on its PeptideMT integration as proof of product readiness. Preserve the original reference and credit; this issue does not select a new public name or promise a release.

## Review scope and completion criteria

- Map supported and unsupported scientific operations, native AMP/MIC meanings, original token/string distinctions, descriptor definitions, unknown chemistry and failure behavior. Scope the modern inference port separately from unqualified training/analogue routes.
- Review standalone API/CLI usability, explicit configuration/seeds, occurrence identity, structured results, provenance and truthful diagnostics without requiring PeptideMT. Reuse existing owner tests; identify meaningful missing regressions rather than mechanically duplicating them.
- Assess reproducible CPU installation, actual dependency closure/origins, Python/dependency claims, startup/resource controls, offline operation and checkpoint/PCA acquisition. Exact local Python 3.14 execution is not all-platform support or a qualified public installer.
- Audit method/software attribution, original notices, versioning and data/model use boundaries; retain the unresolved starter-versus-original-Drive byte identity and broader redistribution/output-use questions.
- Prepare user documentation, a retained-data example, limitations/model card and a prioritized product backlog. Record observed defects in their owning issues. Machine-readable profile metadata already belongs to #2.
- Finish with an evidence-backed readiness assessment and explicit remaining blockers; packaging/release implementation and publication remain separately authorized actions.

Interest from original authors is a separate collaboration question; useful standalone modernization does not depend on creating a new algorithm.

issues.title: Assess whether HydrAMP can seed a family-extensible peptide-generation method
issues.body:
## Scientific question

Could the modernized approach be a useful starting point for generation for CPP or other peptide families, or for a distinct family-extensible method? This is a feasibility question, not a demonstrated property of the current AMP checkpoint or an approved new architecture.

## Proposed investigation and completion criteria

- Separate reusable software infrastructure (traceable inference, token/occurrence contracts, provider boundaries, controlled experiments) from learned family-specific information and empirical claims.
- Identify which assumptions in representation, conditioning, latent prior, labels/losses and evaluators would have to be revisited. Do not transfer AMP/MIC heads or interpret their scores as another family’s activity without new evidence.
- Inventory candidate family-specific data and terms, assay/chemistry meanings, label consistency, homology/training overlap and evaluation controls before proposing retraining or fine-tuning.
- Compare reuse of the existing approach, a distinct successor and alternative methods on fit to the scientific question. Reuse of code is not by itself a reason to retain an unsuitable model architecture.
- Specify risks of negative transfer, multi-function objectives and invalid/unsupported chemistry, and preserve MolSysMT ownership of molecular-system manipulation.
- Produce a reasoned reuse/adapt/redesign/defer recommendation, with a prospective validation design and ownership. A possible successor would keep its new method identity and claims distinct from a faithful modernization of HydrAMP.

No new-family capability, learned model, training/fine-tuning, data acquisition campaign, feedback route or PeptideMT scientific scope is commissioned by this issue. It retains the investigators’ question for a future decision.

issues.title: Prepare a possible handoff to original HydrAMP authors and assess collaboration interest
issues.body:
## Purpose

Retain the question of whether the original authors would value the modern PyTorch/Python 3.14 inference implementation, and prepare a factual handoff if the investigators later choose to approach them. Their interest is currently unknown. A modern deployment can be useful whether or not we pursue a distinct family-extensible method.

## Preparation and completion criteria

- Assemble a concise, reviewable summary of what was ported and what remains unchanged: original source/assets, equations, weights, token semantics, native route, descriptor definitions and attribution.
- Include installation/runtime evidence, finite sequence/result fidelity, unresolved numerical/global-rank deviations and their explanation, the original’s pointwise advantages, scientific/use limitations and the lack of a demonstrated joint AMP/NonHemo hit on the small H4 pool. Avoid claiming universal equivalence or biological superiority.
- Determine which source, artifacts, tests and results are actually publishable/reviewable. Local dirty worktrees and unpublished wheels must not be described as an available release; retain checkpoint/data licensing and confidentiality boundaries.
- Propose possible cooperation forms (review, upstream contribution, maintained port or independent fork) and responsibility/maintenance questions without promising author endorsement or upstream acceptance.
- Deliver a local proposed recipient/channel and exact sanitized handoff text for investigator review. Record contact/response only if later explicitly authorized, or a reasoned defer/decline disposition.

**No message, upstream issue/comment, PR, email or other contact with the original authors is authorized here.** This issue is in our own fork specifically to preserve the future question. External publication/contact requires the investigators’ explicit permission for the destination and content. Do not infer permission from this issue, credentials or generic reporting duties.
